title: Fat Bear Week: Vote for the Chubbiest Champion!
summary:
What if you could vote for the chubbiest bear in the world? Fat Bear Week is back! From September 22 to 29, 2026, people everywhere can vote for the fattest brown bear at Katmai National Park in Alaska. This is the 12th year of the contest.

Katmai is huge—4.1 million acres of volcanoes, rivers, and forests. About 2,200 brown bears live there. They eat lots of salmon to get ready for winter. The bears need extra fat to survive the long, cold months.

Park Ranger Mike Fitz started Fat Bear Week in 2014. He saw two photos of the same bear—one from June and one from September. The bear looked much bigger in the second photo! That gave him the idea.

In 2025, more than 1.7 million votes came from over 100 countries. This year, 16 bears are competing. One bear, Chunk, is back to defend his title after recovering from a broken jaw. Another, Bucky, can snatch jumping salmon out of the air. Bear 132 is raising three cubs, and one cub got lost this summer but survived alone for days before finding its family again.

You can vote online every day. The champion is crowned on September 29. It's a fun way to cheer for these amazing animals!
why_it_matters: Fat Bear Week shows how a silly online vote can get kids and grown-ups excited about wild animals — and reminds us that bears work hard all autumn just to make it through the winter.

background_read: Katmai National Park is a huge wild park in Alaska (the northernmost U.S. state), where brown bears gather at rivers and waterfalls to catch salmon every summer.
Alaskan brown bears are some of the biggest bears on Earth. In autumn they eat huge amounts so they can sleep through the long, cold winter living off the fat they stored.
Fat Bear Week began as a fun way to teach people about the bears and about the salmon-filled rivers the bears depend on.
Article_Structure: WHO: Park Ranger Mike Fitz, who started the contest in 2014, and 16 bears competing this year, including Chunk, Bucky and Bear 132.
WHAT: People vote online every day for the fattest brown bear, and the champion is crowned on September 29.
WHERE: Katmai National Park in Alaska — 4.1 million acres of volcanoes, rivers and forests, home to about 2,200 brown bears.
WHY: The bears need extra fat from salmon to survive the long, cold winter, and the contest is a fun way to cheer for them.

perspectives.description: They love the contest because it is funny and easy to join, and they enjoy picking a favourite bear and cheering it on.
They think the contest is a smart way to teach millions of people about bears, salmon and the wild places that need protecting.
They say it is mostly a popularity contest, and that the bears' real problems — like fewer salmon and shrinking wild land — get much less attention.
